local_checks.invariant: The source uploaded to Cloud Build and the built image carry no secret (env file, node_modules with secrets, /tmp/env-vars.yaml).

local_checks.invariant: The backend trusts X-Forwarded-For only from the intended ingress chain (Firebase Hosting then Cloud Run front end); a peer that bypasses Firebase cannot choose req.ip.

Raised as needs_validation (hosted front-end XFF behaviour and ingress setting not observable).

local_checks.result: Holds: rewrite to serviceId comptaflow-api in us-east1; CSP script-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS, nosniff. No path in firebase.json exposes secrets.

local_checks.invariant: Developer/agent tooling and dependency updates do not introduce an unreviewed execution path into a privileged CI job.

local_checks.invariant: Independent verification of candidate deploy/cloud-run-public-ingress-forwarded-for-trust-two-hops

x_hardening: deploy-cloud-run.yml line 255-261 runs `npm ci` (all dependency lifecycle scripts plus the prisma postinstall) in the same step that exports the direct production DATABASE_URL; run `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npx prisma generate` in a step without secrets, and expose DATABASE_URL only to `prisma migrate deploy`.

GCP_SA_KEY is a long-lived JSON service-account key (deploy-cloud-run.yml line 265, sauvegarde-base.yml line 338); prefer Workload Identity Federation bound to the main branch / production environment, and separate the deploy identity from the backup-bucket writer.

Third-party actions holding deploy credentials are referenced by mutable tags (FirebaseExtended/action-hosting-deploy@v0 with the Firebase service account, google-github-actions/auth@v2 and setup-gcloud@v2 with GCP_SA_KEY); pin to full commit SHAs and let Dependabot (github-actions ecosystem already configured) bump the SHAs.

requetes-production.yml read-only guarantee rests on PGOPTIONS and a keyword filter; additionally use a dedicated read-only database role for that secret rather than the migration-capable direct endpoint.

.mcp.json pins @magicuidesign/mcp@2.0.0 but its transitive dependencies are resolved unlocked at every `npx -y` launch in developer/agent sessions that may hold repository push credentials; consider a lockfile-backed local install.
The Firebase PR preview job uses the same service account as the live deploy; a preview-only identity limited to preview channels would bound a compromised PR build.

local_checks.invariant: Client-side redirect cannot be steered to an attacker-chosen origin or javascript: scheme.
local_checks.result: The only location write is window.location.replace(redirectionDuSite(location)) (main.tsx:16). It fires only when hostname equals omegax.vmgconsulting.net and returns either '/vitrine/' or the constant 'https://oomega.web.app' concatenated with location.pathname (always beginning with '/'), search and hash, so the destination host is fixed. No open redirect.

local_checks.invariant: The public vitrine script and the service worker expose no DOM sink, cache or interception that could serve one account's data to another.
local_checks.result: vitrine.js writes only through textContent/setAttribute of constant values and a numeric trial duration; its fetch uses credentials 'omit'. sw.js has no fetch handler, caches nothing and deletes all caches on activate, so no response survives logout or account switch.

local_checks.invariant: Browser storage holds no session credential usable after logout and no private response readable by a later account on the same device.
local_checks.result: Session JWT is an httpOnly cookie; localStorage holds only the CSRF token (useless without the cookie, cleared by setCsrf(null) on logout and lost session, auth.tsx:146,190,276), and setCsrf clears the in-memory referentiels cache. Logout also closes the session server-side (POST /auth/logout awaited). dossiersRecents keeps dossier name and login email by design, no secret. Other keys are UI preferences keyed by tenant. No stale-authorization path with a less-trusted reader found.

local_checks.invariant: Credentialed CORS is granted only to named, publisher-controlled origins.
local_checks.result: optionsCors uses a fixed list (oomega.web.app, oomega.firebaseapp.com, omegax.vmgconsulting.net) plus CORS_ORIGIN when NODE_ENV=production; origin reflection (origin:true) only when NODE_ENV is not production. On-site initialiser writes NODE_ENV=production, so the on-site server also uses the fixed list, and its cookie is SameSite=Lax. local_checks.invariant: Hosted and on-site interface CSP blocks inline and third-party script execution.
local_checks.result: Both policies set script-src 'self', object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'; hosted connect-src adds only the two EU telemetry hosts. API responses carry helmet default-src 'none'. No same-origin script gadget found in the SPA sources reviewed.

Function profiles do not isolate every path that puts an entry into the livre-journal: module annulations that inscribe a VALIDEE negative (virements-fonds, remises, effets, titres, operations-tresorerie under TRESORERIE; creances-douteuses under SAISIE) and DeclarationDeviseANouveauService.declarer (VALIDEE correction when doubleRegardValidation is off, under STRUCTURE) succeed for a COMPTABLE whose profile omits VALIDATION. local_checks.invariant: Every Prisma operation on a cloisonne model is bound to the session tenant by value (collections), re-read before unit writes, verified after unit reads, and creations/updates cannot move a row to another tenant
local_checks.result: filtreBorne checks the tenantId VALUE (equals/in only), rejects NOT/none/isNot/every and partial OR; rule B re-reads the owner through the current transaction; rule A nulls foreign unit reads and injects tenantId into narrow selects; rule D/E check data.tenantId and tenant.connect. No bypass of the top-level row found. The extension does NOT inspect scalar foreign keys in data (compteId, tiersId, ...), nested writes, or rows returned by include/select of relations; when the where is bound (rule A short-circuit at line 349) the result is returned unchecked. Isolation of related rows therefore depends entirely on each service validating body-supplied FK ids.

Two are not: CreerDemandeDto.tiersId in circularisation (stored unvalidated and later returned via include tiers {code, nom}) and CreerCompteDto/ModifierCompteDto.tauxTvaDefautId in compte.service (spread into data unvalidated; no read path returning the foreign TauxTva found, so hardening only).

local_checks.invariant: Independent verification of candidate circularisation/creerDemande:tiersId-not-bound-to-tenant
local_checks.result: needs_validation: No OS-enforced sandbox on the audit host for this run: the compiled server was not executed against two dummy tenants, so the cross-tenant code/nom disclosure is source-inferred, not observed.

x_hardening: CompteService.creer and modifier spread dto.tauxTvaDefautId into compte data without a tenant-bound TauxTva lookup (src/modules/comptes/compte.service.ts lines 247-260 and 505); no read path returning the foreign TauxTva was found (EcritureService checks tauxTvaId against the tenant at line 1147, and the FK is ON DELETE SET NULL), so the effect is a dangling cross-tenant reference only. Validate it like TauxTvaService.verifierComptes does for its accounts.

The cloisonnement extension guards the top-level row only; it never verifies scalar foreign keys in create/update data, nested relation writes, or rows returned through include/select of relations. A generic guard (e.g. verifying that every included cloisonne row carries the session tenantId, or validating FK ids of cloisonne targets on create/update) would turn the per-service discipline into an engine guarantee, as the module's own header intends.

Rule A returns null when an unbound findFirst first matches a foreign row even if a same-tenant row also matches; this fails closed (no leak) but can make a service believe a record is absent. Requiring a bound where for findFirst on cloisonne models would remove the ambiguity.

AuditContexteInterceptor returns without any tenant context when request.user.email is absent; with no dossier the extension lets unit reads through unchecked and accepts any literal tenantId on collections. No authenticated user without email was found, but the guard would be stronger failing closed when a user is present without a tenant.

local_checks.invariant: Every /plateforme route requires JwtAuthGuard + OperateurPlateformeGuard: DB-reloaded estOperateurPlateforme, active TOTP, and a full (password+code) login under 8 h.
local_checks.result: Holds as written: controller-level @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, OperateurPlateformeGuard) covers all 22 console routes; flag and 2FA state are reloaded from the DB per request (jwt.strategy.ts:190-191); connexionComplete is only minted by login, register, and TOTP activate/deactivate (auth.service.ts:275,523,635,649). The guard does not bind the operator to any tenant and checks only the account's current flag, so its assurance reduces to how the flag and the account's credentials are obtained (see candidates).

local_checks.invariant: The operator flag is granted only to an account whose control of the listed address was proven (handed-over lead from h01).
local_checks.result: Fails: onModuleInit promotes any account whose stored email exactly equals a listed address (plateforme.service.ts:75-79), on every instance boot; the stored email is never verified on any door that sets it (changerAdresse auth.service.ts:744-760; POST /utilisateurs utilisateur.service.ts:67-80 with admin-chosen password; creerCellule groupe.service.ts:472-497 returns the temp password). Grant-only design plus the comment that unknown addresses are promoted when later created make pre-listed or vacated addresses claimable. Whether the deployed list currently contains an unclaimed address is not source-visible.

local_checks.result: composer (relances.service.ts:709-740) uses sequential String.replace with string replacements built from tiers name, entity name and ecriture libelles; the template (niveau.modeleTexte) is written by ADMIN_CABINET only (relances.controller.ts:23-30) and emission is ADMIN_CABINET/COMPTABLE (:60-61). x_hardening: src/modules/relances/relances.service.ts:728-739 and src/modules/remises/remise-en-banque.ts:242-251 render templates with chained String.prototype.replace(regex, string): user values (tiers name, ecriture libelle, cheque reference, titulaire, dossier/banque name) are interpreted as replacement patterns ('$&', '$`', "$'", '$$'), and a value containing a later token (e.g. a dossier or bank named '{lignes}' or a tiers named '{detail}') is expanded by the following pass. Effect is limited to reshuffling text already in the same letter/bordereau, written by the same tenant principals, so no boundary is crossed; use a single-pass function replacer as tiers/modeles-impression.ts:193 does (modele.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (b, n) => valeurs[n] ?? b)) and add a regression case with a libelle of "$`" and a tiers named '{detail}'.

Mail subject for relances includes the entity name joined with '\n' (relances.service.ts:802, 889); header safety rests entirely on nodemailer folding/encoding. Normalising CR/LF to spaces in objetDeLaRelance and in destinataireNom before enqueue would make the invariant source-visible rather than library-dependent.

local_checks.invariant: An anonymously deposited licence file is accepted only if Ed25519-signed by the hard-coded VMG public key over a canonical serialisation, bound to this machine fingerprint, and no crypto failure falls back to acceptance
local_checks.result: verifierLicence validates content shape, verifies Ed25519 over serialiser() (fixed key order) with the constant public key (never read from env), treats any verify exception as SIGNATURE_INVALIDE, then checks machine fingerprint, clock rollback, expiration and maintenance date. deposer() only writes a file whose verdict is VALIDE and refuses an older emiseLe than the current valid licence. No fallback-to-accept path found.

local_checks.invariant: Backup and dossier-creation routes are reachable only by the ADMIN_CABINET of the first (installation) tenant on an on-site install; anonymous /sur-site routes expose no tenant data and are inert in hosted mode
local_checks.result: The four reserved routes carry JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard and AdministrateurInstallationGuard in that order; the guard refuses when not SUR_SITE, when role is not ADMIN_CABINET, or when tenantId differs from the oldest tenant (dossierDInstallation). /sur-site/etat returns {surSite:false} in hosted mode and /sur-site/licence throws BadRequest there. Anonymous etat discloses licence holder, number and machine fingerprint only (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: External backup copies use authenticated encryption with a fresh nonce per file, a slow KDF, and never leave partially decrypted or plaintext output on failure
local_checks.result: AES-256-GCM with randomBytes(12) IV per file, scrypt N=2^15 r=8 p=1 with 16-byte random salt, tag appended and checked via setAuthTag; decryption writes to .partiel and unlinks on failure, renames only on success; recopier refuses to copy when no key is configured (no plaintext fallback). Phrase read from TTY, not argv. Derived key is stored on the poste next to plaintext local copies, documented by design.

local_checks.invariant: An application-level installation admin can choose a backup destination without making the Windows service (LocalSystem) touch arbitrary local paths or authenticate to arbitrary network hosts
local_checks.result: definirCopieExterne accepts any absolute path including UNC (only isAbsolute + existsSync + test write), and the service runs under LocalSystem (WinSW without a declared account). existsSync/writeFileSync/chiffrerFichier on a \\host\share path make the machine account authenticate over SMB to an attacker-chosen host, repeated hourly by recopierSiAbsente. Candidate needs_validation (Windows/AD behaviour not source-visible, no sandbox).

local_checks.invariant: Security-critical secrets (TOTP secret, backup codes, on-site DB password and JWT secret) come from a CSPRNG and secret comparisons are constant-time

No weak randomness found.

x_hardening: Licence anti-rollback in LicenceSurSiteService.deposer compares only emiseLe, so any anonymous LAN client holding another VMG-signed licence for the same machine with an equal or later emiseLe (e.g. a shorter-lived or lower dossiersMax one) can replace the installed one via POST /sur-site/licence; consider requiring authentication (installation admin) once a valid licence exists.

GET /sur-site/etat anonymously returns licence holder name, licence number, machine fingerprint and premierDossierAttendu to any LAN client; acceptable for first-run UX but could be reduced to statut/empreinte once a tenant exists.
The clock-rollback guard relies on horloge.json under DOSSIER_DONNEES, which local Windows administrators can delete; this is licensing enforcement only, not a cross-principal boundary.

The external-copy AES key is derived once and stored (with its salt) in sauvegarde-externe.json on the same disk as the plaintext local dumps; documented design, protected only by the ACL set in initialiser.ps1.
pg_dump stderr is returned verbatim in the BadRequest of SauvegardeSurSiteService.executer to the installation admin; it does not include PGPASSWORD (passed by env) but may reveal host paths.

AdministrateurInstallationGuard derives the installation tenant as the oldest Tenant row; on a fresh install the first /auth/register after the licence is deposited (open to the LAN) becomes installation admin, and two concurrent registrations can both pass premierDossierAttendu (count==0). The register route itself is owned by h01; noted here because the guard's trust depends on it.
TOTP secrets (User.secretDoubleAuth) are stored unencrypted in the database column; acceptable given DB access control but an application-level encryption key would limit exposure of a database dump.
